sections.title: The Role
paras: We're looking for a Staff Product Marketing Manager to own the Onboard & Build stage of the customer lifecycle — the moment a developer (or their agent) first meets CockroachDB and decides whether to build on it. It's the front door of our entire go-to-market motion: if we don't win here, nothing downstream matters.

You'll own four connected user journeys end-to-end — Activation to Collaboration, Data Onboarding & Enablement, Developer Experiences, and Programmability & Extensibility — as a single, coherent stage rather than four disconnected pieces. That's deliberate: the developer's path from “curious” to “building in production” should feel like one story, and you're the person who makes it one.

This is a senior, high-ownership role. You'll set the positioning, build the messaging, and drive the enablement and content for how developers adopt CockroachDB — including the AI-native patterns increasingly defining this stage: agent-driven discovery, MCP and agent-facing surfaces, and the reality that coding agents themselves now evaluate and choose databases. You'll sit inside Product Marketing & DevRel within the R&D organization, close to engineering and on the roadmap early enough to shape the story, not just narrate it.
bullets: Activation to Collaboration. The front line of the agentic strategy — how developers and their coding agents discover, evaluate, and choose CockroachDB. If an agent doesn't pick us at activation, nothing downstream happens; you own making sure we're the obvious choice.

Data Onboarding & Enablement. The migration and onboarding story — how teams move off legacy databases and get to production, including the AI Migration Assistant and the MOLT tooling that de-risks the path.
Developer Experiences. The end-to-end developer experience — quickstarts, docs, sample apps, and the surfaces that turn first-touch curiosity into a running application.

Programmability & Extensibility. How developers extend and build on CockroachDB — the interfaces, integrations, and capabilities (SQL Server design partnerships, Dynamic SQL, and more) that make it a platform, not just a database.

sections.title: You Will
bullets: Positioning & messaging for the stage. Build the message house for Onboard & Build — the value propositions, proof points, and narrative that make developers choose and stay. Keep all four journeys laddering to one coherent story and to the broader company positioning.

Launch & GTM execution. Own the PMM deliverables for launches touching your journeys — messaging, enablement, content, and field readiness — mapped to the GTM readiness plan and shipped on time. You move fast once positioning locks.

Field & sales enablement. Arm the field to sell the onboarding and developer story — first-call decks, objection handling, competitive framing, and the pitch reps carry — partnering with the enablement team on delivery.

The AI-native adoption story. Own how the agentic era shows up at this stage: agent-driven discovery, agents as a first-class audience, and the message that CockroachDB is where developers and their agents build. Turn it into proof, not just positioning.

Cross-functional partnership. Work hand-in-glove with the PMs for each journey, with DevRel, docs, and demand gen — translating what's shipping into what the market hears, and bringing developer reality back into the roadmap.
Proof and content. Drive the case studies, reference stories, and technical content that make the onboarding and build story credible — grounded in real customer outcomes, not claims.

sections.title: The Expectations
bullets: In your first 30 days, you'll go deep on the product and the four journeys, meet the PMs and cross-functional partners you'll work with, and audit the existing positioning, messaging, and content across Onboard & Build for gaps and quick wins.

By 60 days, you'll have a clear point of view on where the stage's story is strong and where it's thin, shipped your first messaging or enablement deliverable, and begun driving one of the four journeys end-to-end.

By 90 days, you'll own the full Onboard & Build narrative — a coherent message house across all four journeys, active field enablement, and a working partnership with the journey PMs feeding the roadmap.

sections.title: You Have
bullets: 8+ years in product marketing, with a track record of owning positioning, messaging, and launches for technical products — ideally databases, developer tools, data infrastructure, or cloud platforms (Staff level; senior candidates with exceptional depth considered).

Genuine technical fluency. You can hold a real conversation with developers and PMs about distributed systems, databases, and how software gets built — and translate it into messaging that's both accurate and compelling. You don't fake the technical depth; you have it.

Fluency in the AI-native developer world. You understand how developers build with LLMs and agents today — RAG, vector search, agent memory, MCP, agent-driven workflows — and can position data infrastructure credibly within it.

A clear, opinionated point of view. You bring a strong PMM perspective and defend it with evidence. You'd rather challenge a weak positioning than execute it quietly, and you know how to disagree constructively.

W&B Models is the experiment tracking platform used by the world's leading AI teams, from frontier labs training foundation models to enterprise teams fine-tuning for production. Researchers live in it daily: logging runs, comparing training curves, debugging divergences, building reports, and deciding what to try next.

As Senior Product Manager for Models, you'll drive improvements across the core experiment workflow: how researchers design experiments, visualize what's happening inside them, monitor long-running training jobs, and analyze results across hundreds or thousands of runs. You'll do this at a moment when autoresearch and agentic workflows are reshaping what that loop looks like. Your job is to deeply understand how modern ML research actually gets done and make the inner loop of hypothesis → run → analysis → next run dramatically faster and more insightful. That loop looks…

sections.title: About the Role
paras: This role reports to the Director of Product Management and partners closely with engineering, design, and teams across W&B and CoreWeave.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Advance the researcher's daily workflow. Experiment tracking is where researchers spend their days (and nights). You'll drive the roadmap for how runs are organized, compared, and understood, with a relentless focus on the questions researchers need to answer.

Rethink how training is visualized and monitored. Modern training runs are long, expensive, and failure-prone. You'll shape how W&B surfaces what matters mid-run — loss curves, system metrics, evals, anomalies — so teams catch problems early and understand their models more deeply, across web and mobile.

Make analysis at scale a first-class experience. As experiments grow from dozens of runs to thousands, the hard problems shift from logging to sense-making. You'll define how researchers slice, aggregate, and reason across large experiment histories, including where AI-assisted analysis can do work humans currently do by hand.

Ground every decision in how researchers actually work. You'll spend real time with users, from frontier lab researchers to individual practitioners, and translate what you learn into product decisions the whole team can rally behind.

Ship with quality and speed. You'll own execution from problem definition through launch and iteration, using usage data and customer feedback to guide each stage. W&B's users are discerning; polish and performance are features.

You know what it feels like to babysit a training run, debug a loss spike at 2am, or dig through a hundred runs to figure out which ablation mattered.
You have 3+ years of product management experience on technical products for developer or researcher audiences, with a track record of shipping products users love.

You have strong instincts for data visualization and product design. You can reason about what makes a chart, dashboard, or comparison view genuinely useful vs. merely present, and you sweat the details of how information is displayed.

You reach for AI tools instinctively. Claude, Codex, and agentic workflows are how you work: for prototyping, analysis, and exploring ideas. You're excited to build products for people who work the same way.
You're technically fluent. You can read a training script, discuss evaluation methodology, and hold your own in architecture conversations with engineers.
You communicate with clarity and precision , keeping engineering, design, and go-to-market stakeholders aligned without ceremony.

paras: “With great power comes great responsibility.” Uncle Ben

Thanx has reorganized around AI. Claude Code is in daily use in every function, and every employee has an unlimited token budget. We didn’t stop at handing people tools. We built the internal systems that turn customer voice into shipped product, and we keep tightening that loop:
bullets: Customer voice is queryable. Agents do real engineering work. Our agent fleet picks up specified features and bugs, opens root-caused, review-ready pull requests, reviews human PRs, and improves its own skills based on how its PRs fared. Engineers stay accountable for everything that merges.

Prioritization runs on signal, not volume. Every initiative carries explicit conviction from CS, sales, marketing, finance, partnerships, product, and data, so the roadmap reflects where the business is actually pulling.
